THE ONE FORCED DEVIATION FROM THE INK - S44 (423,724): the y~722 rail's left tip lands squarely on column 3's lower vertical (inkmap at (427,724) shows a continuous vertical with the rail's blob-tipped left end merged into it - it reads as a plain T). Taken literally, that ties the rail to column 3's bottom section, which runs unbroken down to the bottom rail at (427,858) (verified by a column scan y=700..860) and hence to net 0 - and the 15V source's bottom is on that same bottom rail via the (868,860) corner, so the 15V V-DC would have both terminals on net 0, a short-circuited voltage source (and the 10A source would also sit 0-to-0). Electrical impossibility overrides the ink prior, so I severed the rail from column 3 here, expressed as S44 = [[79,86]] (column above e79 joined to column below e86; the rail edge e82 joined to neither), which leaves the column intact on net 0 and puts the rail on n5 with the 10A bottom and the 15V top. Severing the rail's other end at S43 instead gives exactly the same terminal partition, so the choice of end does not affect the netlist. Note explicitly what the literal reading would have implied: #11.t0 and #8.t1 would join net 0 (6 nets instead of 7) with the 15V source shorted. Note also the pattern this deviation breaks: the y~550 rail's left tip lands the same way on column 2's lower vertical (S35), which I did NOT sever because it creates no impossibility - it simply grounds the 5V/10A tap. So on this sheet the two lower rails are drawn overshooting the column they hop over and terminating on the previous column's lower (grounded) section; only the second one had to be broken to keep the netlist electrically possible.
